rounds.review: Seventeen real brand marks from Academicons 1.9.4 under SIL OFL 1.1, with the licence shipped in LICENSES.md and the reserved name unused, as that licence requires. The six services Academicons does not cover -- OpenAlex, Europe PMC, medRxiv, ChemRxiv, Lens.org, Harzing -- are drawn here in the same stroke family and are deliberately not imitations of anyone's trademark. Each mark keeps its own viewBox, because these come from a font and forcing them into one box would squash every non-square one.
rounds.verification: Node/DOM tests, an offline render of the real workbench DOM and CSS, and the in-Zotero self-check against the user's own library.

rounds.title: 저자를 통계 한 줄이 아니라 사람으로
rounds.gap: A followed author was a name and four numbers. PostGrabbit already showed the user a face and the people around each PI, and that is what makes a person easier to hold in mind than a row of statistics.
rounds.entryPoint: 연구 작업 패널 → 저자 추적 → 저자 열기

tests.name: a colleague's headshot on the same page is not taken for the author
two equally good candidates are refused rather than guessed
the plugin can never be talked into fetching something off this machine
a co-author network is the people actually on the papers, ranked by how often
an author is shown as a person, with the people they publish with

rounds.review: The portrait rules are PostGrabbit's, kept rather than reinvented: a candidate must be named on the page, a logo or banner is never a person, and an ambiguous winner is refused outright. One hole was closed on the way over -- on a lab page under /people/, an image whose own alt text names a colleague could win the weakest rule and be served up as the author. The co-author network costs no request at all: the works the tab already fetched carry every authorship, and an edge exists because two names are on the same paper.
rounds.verification: Node/DOM tests, an offline render of the real workbench DOM and CSS, and the in-Zotero self-check against the user's own library.

rounds.title: 키가 없으면 실패할 수밖에 없는 버튼을 먼저 내밀지 않기
rounds.gap: The journals tab led with an easyScholar grade lookup. The user never had that key -- it is in neither the Zotero profile nor their Aside vault -- so the first button offered could only produce an error.
rounds.entryPoint: 연구 작업 패널 → 저널 지표

tests.name: all tabs expose functional primary actions and use library service contracts

rounds.review: The route that needs no key comes first, and the easyScholar button appears only once a key exists. Without one the tab says what the key would add rather than offering a control that cannot work.
rounds.verification: Node/DOM tests, an offline render of the real workbench DOM and CSS, and the in-Zotero self-check against the user's own library.

rounds.title: 보충자료 판별을 파일 이름이 아니라 내용으로
rounds.gap: The rule looked at filenames -- mmc1.pdf, MOESM1_ESM.pdf, s1.pdf. Measured against this library it flagged 1 attachment out of 1,229, because ZotMoov has renamed every file to 'Author - Year - Title.pdf' and the publisher's name is gone. The badge showed 7 items; the library actually has 29 supplementary files, 17 duplicates and 6 papers filed under the wrong item.
rounds.entryPoint: Files 열 · 우클릭 → 첨부파일 종류 판별

tests.name: a supplementary file is recognised by what it says, not what it is called
the same document attached twice is a duplicate, not a second supplement
a different paper filed under this item is called out
markup in a Zotero title does not turn a correctly filed paper into somebody else's
the files cell tells a supplement, a duplicate and a mis-filed paper apart

rounds.review: Zotero already extracts every PDF's text for its own search index, so reading the first page costs nothing and needs no PDF parser. A supplementary file says so in its opening words; an article carries a masthead, a section label or a DOI line. Three things turn up as 'an extra PDF' and they are not the same -- a supplement, the same file twice, and a different paper filed here by mistake -- and calling all three 'SI x2' is what made the badge not worth looking at. Two measured corrections: the title check reads the whole document rather than page one, because a first page often opens with the abstract and never repeats the title (a Nature Chemical Biology review scored 43% and was called foreign); and Zotero titles carry markup, so BREX made twelve correctly filed papers look like somebody else's. The 0.70 threshold is read off the distribution over all 1,211 attachments with text: 1,186 use every word of their title, everything below 0.70 is a real filing mistake, and nothing sits in between.
rounds.verification: Run live in Zotero over the user's own 1,223 attachments: 1,170 article, 29 supplementary, 17 duplicate, 6 different-paper, 1 unknown -- matching the offline prediction exactly.

rounds.title: Zotero가 아직 읽지 않은 첨부는 색인부터
rounds.gap: Eleven attachments had no extracted text, so the scan could not judge them at all and simply reported them as unknown.
rounds.entryPoint: 우클릭 → 첨부파일 종류 판별

tests.name: a file Zotero has not indexed is indexed first, not written off
a scan can be told not to index, and then simply reports what it could not read

rounds.review: Asking Zotero to index them is the same extraction its own search does, and turns 'cannot tell' into an answer. The option to skip it was called `index`, which the enclosing loop counter shadowed -- 0 !== false, so every scan indexed regardless of what the caller asked; the test that was written to prove the option worked is what found it.
rounds.verification: Contrast measured numerically for every colour in both schemes, rendered offline from the real stylesheet, and checked live in Zotero.

rounds.title: 전체 색감을 파스텔로
rounds.gap: The colours were loud and uneven: against white, gold sat at 2.1 contrast and blue at 4.7, so one badge shouted while another was hard to read. That unevenness is what made a row look garish rather than the hues themselves.
rounds.entryPoint: 문헌 목록의 모든 열 · 연구 작업 패널 · ZotPoP 검색 창

tests.name: every badge colour lands on the same contrast, so no one of them shouts
light and dark semantic text, muted metadata and selected navigation meet normal-text contrast

rounds.review: The hue stays, the saturation drops to about a third, and the lightness of every colour is chosen so they all land within 0.5 of the same contrast against the surface behind them -- evenness is the point. The softness lives in the fills: the pill tint is raised from 0.13 to 0.20 in light and 0.20 to 0.26 in dark, rather than the ink being washed out. Three colours had to stay deeper than the family because they carry text on themselves: the accent under a white label, and the error ink on its own wash. A dead rule matching a colour nothing has emitted for a long time went with it.
rounds.verification: Contrast measured numerically for every colour in both schemes, rendered offline from the real stylesheet, and checked live in Zotero.

rounds.title: 이미 가진 보충자료를 다시 받지 않기
rounds.gap: The downloader decided 'already have it' by comparing publisher filenames against what was attached. A file mover renames those away, so all twenty-nine supplements in this library looked absent and would have been fetched again as duplicates.
rounds.entryPoint: 우클릭 → 보충자료 내려받기

tests.name: a paper whose supplement is already on the shelf is not fetched again
a supplement that was just downloaded is badged without waiting for a scan

rounds.review: It asks the content scan instead, which knows what each file is whatever it is called, and skips the paper without spending a request. A file that arrives from the supplementary endpoint records its verdict as it lands, so the badge is right immediately rather than after the next sweep.
rounds.verification: Verified live: the scan holds 29 supplements, every one of which the downloader now skips.

rounds.title: 보충자료만 들어 있는 문헌 찾아 원논문에 붙이기
rounds.gap: Twenty-two items in this library are a supplement filed as its own bibliography entry, disconnected from the paper it belongs to. Only five say so in the title; the rest are invisible without reading the file.
rounds.entryPoint: 연구 작업 → 첨부 → 보충자료만 있는 문헌

tests.name: a supplement's home paper is suggested only when the answer is not a guess
the supplement marker comes off a title without taking the title with it
rehoming a supplement moves it and retires only an empty stub

rounds.review: The pairing is a suggestion the user confirms one at a time, never a bulk action. Two things make a wrong guess easy: a short generic title ('Cell-free gene expression') matches almost any document, and a library often holds two papers by one group on one molecule. So a candidate needs five distinct long words to count at all, has to beat the runner-up by a clear margin, and a match found in body text is held to a higher bar than one found in the title -- a supplement cites its neighbours, and one here matched a different paper by the same group on the same enzyme, fully, from a sentence in its methods. Tightening that turned three wrong confident answers into one honest 'I don't know'. Moving a supplement retires the stub only when nothing else is left on it, and only into Zotero's trash.
rounds.verification: Verified live: 22 orphans found, 11 with a confident home.

rounds.title: 받기 전에 몇 편이나 받을 수 있는지 먼저 세기
rounds.gap: The download was a blind sweep. Measured over this library: of 1,146 papers with a DOI, 697 are in PMC, 506 of those have supplementary material, and only 336 are open access -- the only set whose archive the endpoint hands over. A sweep over everything spends a thousand requests to fetch a few hundred files and says nothing about which.
rounds.entryPoint: 우클릭 → 보충자료 → 먼저 확인만

tests.name: the download is counted before it is started, and closed articles are not attempted

rounds.review: One search request per paper answers the question first and costs no downloads at all. A paper that already has its supplement, and one with neither DOI nor title, are answered without asking anything.
rounds.verification: Coverage measured directly against Europe PMC for all 1,146 DOIs in the library.

rounds.title: 관심 저자의 이동은 논문이 아니라 저자 기록에서 읽기
rounds.gap: A move was read off the papers: first the institution on the newest authorship, then every institution across the window. Live, that reported seven, then six, moves among 109 followed authors, and not one was a move -- a second appointment (Harvard and the Broad), an institute inside the university (QB3 in Berkeley), a school named after it (Harvard Medical School), the same place spelled two ways (DTU, 'UC berkely', 'MIT chemistry').
rounds.entryPoint: 관심 저자 → 카드의 소속 줄 · 백필의 관심 저자 단계

tests.name: a move is read from the author record, so a second appointment or a renamed place is not one
moves recorded by the first rule are retired when the store loads

rounds.review: One request per fifty authors reads OpenAlex's own list of current appointments, each with a ROR and the years it was signed. The first sweep adopts OpenAlex's name for the place the author was followed with and keeps the typed text; a move is when every remembered appointment has left that list, dated from the record. Live after the change: 109 records read, 0 moves, 73 authors with more than one appointment, 69 typed places replaced by canonical ones. Moves made by the earlier rules are retired when the store loads.

rounds.title: 저널 프로필: JCR 페이지처럼, 로그인 없이
rounds.gap: The journals tab was a list of names with a figure, and the user asked for what JCR's journal page shows -- each fact with its own sign, and the list by field. JCR's site needs an institutional login, so nothing could be read from it here; the registry shipped with the plugin knows the figure, quartile, abbreviation, publisher and ISSN, and OpenAlex knows the subject fields, h-index, output, open-access status, fee, country and homepage.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 저널 → 저널 이름 클릭

tests.name: a journal opens into a profile of signed facts, and the fields filter the list
cached figures are given their profiles fifty at a time, and the rest marked as asked

rounds.review: The profile fields ride on the request the figure already costs; journals cached before them are filled fifty at a time by ISSN -- 258 journals in this library in six requests, every one with a subject field afterwards. On the tab: the figure in its own column, quartile chip, field chips that filter, a grouped-by-field view with ranks, and a profile under any name with twelve signed facts and a button to the JCR page itself.

rounds.title: 관심 저자의 특허, 키가 있을 때만
rounds.gap: The user chose patents as the third tier of watching an author: a filing is the earliest public sign of where a lab is heading, often a year before the paper. PatentsView, which answered without a key, was retired into the USPTO Open Data Portal in 2025; Europe PMC's patent index stops in 2012; EPO and Lens need keys too. So the tier needs a free USPTO key, and without one it must say so rather than fail.
rounds.entryPoint: 설정 → 지표 → USPTO Open Data Portal 키 · 관심 저자 카드의 특허 배지

sources.marker: patents: the USPTO key, if any, is accepted

tests.name: patents are read from the portal's shape and from PatentsView's, and namesakes are told apart
patents run only with a USPTO key, take the first look as the baseline, and mark what appears later

rounds.review: One request per followed author, at most weekly, the key sent to api.uspto.gov only. The reader accepts the portal's field names and PatentsView's, so a rename degrades to nothing found; namesakes are told apart by the LAST; FIRST form the portal writes. The first look is the baseline; later ones badge the card with what is new, and the detail lists each patent with a link to its public page. No key was available in this session, so the live response shape is unverified: the self-check's patents entry runs one real query the moment a key is entered and reports what came back.

rounds.title: 종류별로 한 번에 가르기: 특허·학위논문·프리프린트
rounds.gap: Patents and theses sat among the papers with only a chip on the tree row; the user asked for them to be a layer of their own. Zotero's tree cannot group, and the panel's type filter was a select of raw itemType names.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 검색줄 아래 종류 칩

tests.name: the library splits by kind with one chip: patents and theses apart from the papers

rounds.review: A row of chips under the search line counts the library by kind -- 논문 1167 · 프리프린트 26 · 학위논문 6 -- and one click shows only that kind; the select says the same in the same words, and each card names its kind unless it is a plain paper. The journal figure takes the same colour bands as the IF column in the tree.

rounds.title: 지도의 범례와 카드의 저널 표식
rounds.gap: The citation map paints every node in its journal's colour, and a reader new to it has no way to know that lilac is Nature and coral is Cell. The explore cards named the journal in plain grey text while the tree, the related list and the journals tab all showed its mark.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 관계 그래프 · 보유 문헌 카드

tests.name: the map names its commonest journals in their own colours, and a card wears its journal mark

rounds.review: Under the map's summary line, the six commonest journals in it, each in its own mark with how many nodes it accounts for; the older tag/author graph now carries venues too, so it is coloured and legended alike. Every explore card wears its journal's mark before the venue, the same mark the tree and the map use.

rounds.title: 전체 화면 토글과 제목 마크업
rounds.gap: The panel floats at a dragged-out size, which on a laptop leaves the list in a letterbox; the user asked for full screen. Titles with Zotero's inline markup showed "Bacillus subtilis" as text.
rounds.entryPoint: 패널 머리줄의 전체 화면 버튼 · 제목줄 더블클릭

tests.name: one press fills the window, the next puts the panel back, and the choice is remembered
markup in a title is drawn as italics and subscripts, not shown as tags

rounds.review: One press fills the window edge to edge, the next puts the panel back, double-clicking the title bar does the same, and the choice is remembered. Six inline tags (i, b, em, strong, sub, sup) are drawn as what they mean wherever the panel writes text; anything else stays literal, and attributes get the plain words.

rounds.title: 분야를 큰 것부터 층층이 고르기
rounds.gap: Twenty-six field chips lay flat in one row, unordered by size. The user asked for the hierarchy arranged large to small and picked level by level.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 저널 → 대분류·분야·세부 분야 칩

tests.name: a journal opens into a profile of signed facts, and the fields filter the list

rounds.review: OpenAlex's topic hierarchy (domain > field > subfield) is kept on each journal's profile; profiles filled before it are asked once more. One chip row per level, largest first; a chosen row folds to its choice with the way back beside it, and the next level opens beneath. Grouping follows the level under the choice.

rounds.title: 논문 함께 읽기: 주장·논리 흐름·논쟁 여지
rounds.gap: The comparison table put papers side by side as fields. The user wanted the model to read them together: each one's claim and the chain it argues along, and where they pull against each other.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 논문 비교 → 함께 읽기

tests.name: reading papers together sends two to six abstracts with their notes, and refuses less or more
the comparison table reads its papers together and keeps the reading as a note

rounds.review: Two to six selected papers -- titles, abstracts, the reader's own notes -- go to the configured AI service with a fixed outline: core claim, line of argument as an arrow chain, strength and limits of the evidence, common ground, every point of contention with the evidence that would settle it, open questions. It is asked not to invent and to say where abstracts are silent. The outline comes back editable, copyable, and can be kept as a note on the first paper.

rounds.title: 관심 저자 목록 관리
rounds.gap: A hundred cards are for noticing news, not for tending the list: nothing let the user find one author, sort by who was checked longest ago, or let one go without opening the card.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 저자 추적 → 목록 관리

tests.name: the followed list can be tended as a table: found, sorted, let go

rounds.review: A table of the followed authors: name, place (with what was typed when followed in the tooltip, shaded when they moved), last check, new papers, patents, and an unfollow button on each row; found by name or place, sorted by news, name, place, longest unchecked or most recently followed; the whole list copyable.

rounds.title: 문헌 트리와 ZotPoP에서도 제목의 기울기
rounds.gap: The panel drew a title's markup, but the tree column and ZotPoP's list still printed "Bacillus subtilis" as text, and ZotPoP imported the plain words, losing the italics for good.
rounds.entryPoint: 문헌 트리 제목 열 · ZotPoP 결과 목록

tests.name: the tree draws the italics and subscripts of a title instead of its tags

rounds.review: The tree's title cell is rebuilt with the six inline tags drawn whenever the tree prints them again; ZotPoP keeps the source's markup beside the plain title, draws it in the list and the detail, and imports it as Zotero itself would.

rounds.title: 함께 읽기 지시문과 새 소식만 보기
rounds.gap: The read-together outline was fixed, while the remark and tag prompts could be changed; and a hundred quiet author cards hid the ten with news.
rounds.entryPoint: 설정 → 번역·AI → 함께 읽기 지시문 · 저자 추적 → 새 소식만

tests.name: the reader can replace the outline for reading together; the language and the no-invention rule stay
one chip keeps only the followed authors with something new

rounds.review: A setting replaces the outline; the output language and the no-invention rule are always appended. A chip on the followed list keeps only the people with a new paper, a new patent or a move.

rounds.title: 패널을 Zotero 탭에 넣기
rounds.gap: The panel floated over the window; the user asked whether it could sit in a tab like a reader.
rounds.entryPoint: 패널 머리줄의 탭 버튼

tests.name: the panel can live in a Zotero tab, remembers it, and comes back when the tab closes

rounds.review: Zotero_Tabs.add gives a tab and a container; the same panel element moves into it and fills it, with the tab bar as its handle. Closing the tab hides the panel, opening the panel selects the tab, and the choice is remembered so the next open goes straight to a tab. The float button brings it back over the window.

rounds.title: 분야 선택을 한 줄의 세 메뉴로
rounds.gap: The chip rows for the subject hierarchy were still hard to read, and a field could not be picked until a domain was.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 저널 → 대분류 › 분야 › 세부 분야 메뉴

tests.name: a journal opens into a profile of signed facts, and the fields filter the list

rounds.review: One line, three menus, large to small, each listing what lies under the choice to its left with counts, largest first; a smaller level can be picked on its own and the levels above it follow; menus not yet narrowed group their options under the parent, biggest parent first. Each journal's fields sit on one line, each field once with its subfields after it.

rounds.title: 카드 위에 손을 올렸을 때 덜 붙어 보이게
rounds.gap: On hover the checkbox, its word and the two buttons crowded together under the status dot, and the buttons wrapped under the checkbox.
rounds.entryPoint: 보유 문헌 카드에 마우스 올리기

tests.name: a journal opens into a profile of signed facts, and the fields filter the list

rounds.review: The buttons take the figures' place at the far right of the title row while the pointer is on the card; the checkbox keeps its word for the screen reader only; the dot sits further in and the row has more air.

rounds.title: 저널을 표로: 이름은 제 색의 글자로, 열 이름과 검색
rounds.gap: Journal rows were three-line cards, the controls sat far above the field menus, and journals could not be searched apart from the paper search.
rounds.entryPoint: 작업 패널 → 저널

tests.name: a journal opens into a profile of signed facts, and the fields filter the list

rounds.review: A real table: rank, the name in the journal's own colour as text (no box), quartile, abbreviation, house, papers here, fields, and the figure at the edge, with the column names once at the top and the two lookups laid over the row on hover. Facts are gathered once per set of items and typing redraws only the list a beat after the last key, which removed the lag; a title-rule journal now carries its registry quartile too. A search box finds journals by name, abbreviation, publisher or field.
